items.stem: What is the difference between a natural 'hazard' and 'risk'?

options.text: A hazard is the threatening process; risk also depends on exposure and vulnerability of people and property
options.rationale: Correct: risk combines the hazard with who and what is exposed and how vulnerable they are.
They are distinct concepts in disaster science.

options.text: A hazard only exists after people are harmed
options.rationale: A hazard can exist whether or not anyone is harmed.

options.text: Risk is the process and hazard is the harm

items.explanation: Correct: risk combines the hazard with who and what is exposed and how vulnerable they are.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A powerful undersea earthquake at a subduction zone can trigger a tsunami. What is the most direct cause of the tsunami? (Select ONE)

options.text: Sudden vertical displacement of the sea floor pushing the water column
options.rationale: Correct: the abrupt sea-floor movement displaces the water, forming the wave.

options.text: Strong winds blowing across the ocean surface
options.rationale: That drives ordinary waves, not this tsunami.

options.text: The Moon pulling the tide higher that day
options.rationale: Tides are not the cause of a tsunami.
Evaporation does not generate a tsunami.

items.explanation: Correct: the abrupt sea-floor movement displaces the water, forming the wave.

items.stem: Select TWO actions that genuinely reduce disaster risk for a flood-prone town. (Select TWO)

options.text: Installing an early-warning system with clear evacuation routes
options.rationale: Correct: timely warning and evacuation reduce harm.

options.text: Restoring wetlands and improving drainage to absorb floodwater
options.rationale: Correct: natural and engineered drainage lower flood impact.

options.text: Building more homes directly on the floodplain
options.rationale: This increases exposure and therefore risk.

options.text: Removing all monitoring to save money
options.rationale: Removing monitoring raises risk by cutting warning time.

items.explanation: Correct: timely warning and evacuation reduce harm.
